title: Stanford scientists restore cartilage in mice by blocking age-related protein

title: Two-year trial: diet soft drinks match water for weight loss
summary: A two-year randomized trial of 493 adults found diet soft drinks sweetened with aspartame, acesulfame-K, or sucralose produced weight loss comparable to water (4.8 kg vs 3.7 kg), with both groups maintaining reductions and showing no clinically meaningful metabolic differences.
takeaways: Diet beverages lost 4.8 kg vs 3.7 kg for water over 104 weeks
No significant differences in blood pressure, cholesterol, or metabolic biomarkers
Both groups sustained weight loss through year two without behavioral support
Sweetener consumption remained within European Food Safety Authority thresholds
Published in British Journal of Nutrition

title: Incremental lifestyle improvements could significantly extend lifespan
summary: A new study suggests that small improvements in sleep, nutrition, and exercise together could meaningfully increase human lifespan.

title: Meta-analysis finds dairy trans fats pose no heart disease or diabetes risk
summary: A meta-analysis of 22 studies found that naturally occurring trans fats in dairy products do not increase risk of heart disease, stroke, or type 2 diabetes. The distinction is critical—industrial trans fats remain harmful, while dairy trans fats showed no adverse effects.
takeaways: 22-study meta-analysis examined dairy trans fats
10 controlled trials: participants consumed 1.3–13.2g trans fat daily
12 long-term cohorts: up to two decades, no adverse associations
Natural dairy trans fats differ from harmful industrial trans fats

title: Single factor emerges as stronger longevity predictor than diet or exercise
summary: A study published in Sleep Advances found that insufficient sleep (less than seven hours nightly) was a stronger predictor of longevity than diet or exercise when analyzing county-level survey data from 2019 to 2025. takeaways: Insufficient sleep (<7 hours/night) stronger predictor of longevity than diet or exercise
Only smoking had stronger association with life expectancy in first model
County-level US survey data, 2019–2025, controlled for physical inactivity, employment, education
Sleep physiologist Andrew McHill: correlation strength was unexpected
Observational study; cannot prove causation; recommends 7–9 hours nightly

title: Vitamin D analog shows promise in pancreatic cancer clinical trial

Patients receiving paricalcitol + chemotherapy showed more treatment responses
High vitamin D receptor tumors had longest overall survival
Published in Nature Cancer; built on Salk Institute laboratory findings
Targets protective fibrotic environment to sensitize tumors to therapy

title: Gut bacterial compound ImP linked to increased Alzheimer's risk
summary: Scientists at the University of Wisconsin-Madison identified imidazole propionate (ImP), a gut-bacteria-derived molecule, as a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. takeaways: ImP crosses bloodstream into brain, increases abnormal beta-amyloid and tau protein accumulation
43% of study participants carried genetic variation associated with substantially elevated ImP levels
Higher blood ImP concentrations linked to significantly faster cognitive decline

title: Study finds strength training shrinks fat cells in mice within seven days
summary: Seven days of strength training sessions in obese mice triggered shrinkage of visceral fat cells and reactivated fat-burning molecular pathways without overall weight loss.

title: Creatine supplementation builds muscle independent of exercise
summary: Research indicates that creatine supplementation can increase muscle mass even in individuals who do not exercise regularly.

title: MIT study reveals hidden cancer risk in ketogenic diet
summary: MIT researchers found that a ketogenic diet increased small-intestinal tumors in cancer-prone mice through altered intestinal stem cell processing.

title: Seven-Day Fasting Study Reveals Major Metabolic Changes in Human Body
summary: Scientists found that prolonged fasting triggers significant physiological changes, with the most notable effects appearing after three days without food.

title: Keto diet may enhance exercise effectiveness for people with hyperglycemia
summary: A ketogenic diet could unlock the metabolic benefits of exercise for people with elevated blood sugar levels.

title: Leucine boosts cellular energy by protecting mitochondrial proteins
summary: Leucine protects key mitochondrial proteins from destruction, boosting cellular energy production and revealing a new link between nutrition and metabolism.

title: Vitamin D2 supplements may reduce natural vitamin D3 levels, study finds
summary: Research warns that taking vitamin D2 supplements can paradoxically lower the body's naturally-produced vitamin D3 levels.

title: Creatine supplementation increases lean muscle and strength in middle-aged adults even without exercise
summary: A 12-week study of adults ages 45–65 found that creatine monohydrate supplementation (10 grams daily) increased lean tissue and strength gains independent of exercise. When combined with resistance training and a calorie-reduced diet, creatine produced significantly greater strength improvements and
takeaways: Non-exercise group taking creatine gained ~2.4 pounds of lean tissue over 12 weeks
Creatine + exercise group showed greater leg press and bench press strength gains than exercise alone
Creatine + exercise + calorie deficit added ~3 pounds lean tissue while reducing body fat percentage
Study involved 64 healthy adults ages 45–65 over 12 weeks
Published in Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition; led by Dr. Richard Kreider at Texas A&M

title: Creatine supplementation builds muscle mass in middle-aged adults even without structured exercise
summary: A 12-week study from Texas A&M University found that middle-aged adults (45–65) taking creatine gained approximately 2.4 pounds of lean tissue and increased strength without following a structured exercise program. takeaways: Adults ages 45–65 taking 10 grams of creatine daily gained roughly 2.4 pounds of lean tissue over 12 weeks without exercise

summary: Research highlights a performance advantage for athletes from combining sodium bicarbonate with carbohydrate supplementation.

title: Sugar consumption may worsen antibiotic damage to gut microbiome
summary: A study found that eating more sugar while taking antibiotics was linked to greater microbiome disruption and increased harmful bacteria growth.

title: Food science innovations applied to sports nutrition performance
summary: Laboratory food science research is being translated into practical nutritional strategies for endurance athletes.

summary: In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low-risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C was linked to favorable inflammation changes and fewer serious complications.
